items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: That was here when I just got tired... that's where this Chauncey Holland came and asked me to revive my band and he got to binge it for you to finance it.

ctx.x: We once talked about being stranded. If you did lose all your money and all that. There was a German man you would wire for money?

No, I know what you're referring to. This was in Texas. That was in East Bernard. I can't recall his name right now. But not being stranded. He was a friend of mine. He told me whenever you need something, just wire it. But now the time that I actually was stranded was when I was with this Chauncey Holland or Al Travis I think. It was in a little town in Carbondale, Illinois. And there was an old lady there, another lady. She liked me and she liked the band. So we were living with her and we didn't have another…
And you did make out when you got the money somehow?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: Any time a man can sell a band for five nights or six nights in a row and book them in two, three towns at the same time, he's got to be good. Same with Al Travis.

ctx.x: That's a UNDERS, Sondas. You know his first name, don't you? No, sure. Well, then I'm sure you can find that. But these funny things come from the other side. Funny things come up like that, just the same way when we were playing in St. Petersburg, Florida, on that pier that ran out into the waters. We had an arrangement on the sheet of R.B. And as the guy would sell him the sheet of R.B., he would sell him with no pants on. Dink Taylor had to sell him to Dink Taylor to Dink Taylor to Dink Taylor to Dink Taylor…
the glass floor. What about, was Chauncey Holland a good salesman? One of the best.
Any time a man can sell a band for five nights or six nights in a row and book them in two, three towns at the same time, he's got to be good. Same with Al Travis.
